chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Talib, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I, Abu Basir, and Muhammad ibn Imran, the mawla of Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, were in his house in Makkah. Muhammad ibn Imran said, "I heard Abu Abdillah عليه السلام saying: 'We are twelve muhaddathun.'" Abu Basir said to him, "Did you hear it from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام?" So he made him swear once or twice that he had heard it. Then Abu Basir said, "But I heard it from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام."

key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: a well-known narrator in Shia hadith who verifies the transmission in this report
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, cited here as the speaker of the report
key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir عليه السلام, from whom Abu Basir also reports hearing this meaning
key_terms.اثْنَا عَشَرَ: twelve; indicating the fixed number of the Imams
key_terms.سَمِعْتُ: I heard; emphasizing direct audition in transmission
key_terms.مُحَدَّثًا: one spoken to or addressed by the angels; a divinely inspired figure without implying prophethood

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Kafi say about the twelve Imams being muhaddathun?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a transmission affirming that the Imams are twelve and describes them as muhaddathun, those addressed or spoken to by the angels. It reflects an important creedal theme in Shia tradition concerning the number of the Imams and their divinely granted status of knowledge.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahyaa and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Talib, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘I, and Abu Baseer, and Mihran a slave of Abu Ja’farasws were in hisasws house in Makkah. Muhammad Bin Imran said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Weasws are twelve Muhaddith (Whom the Angels discuss with)’. So Abu Baseer said to him, ‘You heard from Abu Abdullahasws?’ So he oathed to him once or twice that he did hear it. Then Abu Baseer said, ‘But I heard it from Abu Ja’farasws’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad have narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from abu Talib from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘Abdallah ibn Mihran who has said the following.

“Once I, abu Basir and Muhammad ibn ‘Imran the slave of abu Ja‘far (a.s.) were in his house in Makka. Muhammad ibn ‘Imran said, “I have heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say, ‘We all twelve of us are Muhaddath (the ones to whom angels speak).” Abu Basir then said, “Did you hear abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say so? He made him to swear one or twice that he has heard so. Abu Basir then said, “However, I have heard it from abu Ja‘far (a.s.).”
